History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male lawyer presents with new-onset intermittent frontal headaches associated with palpitations, intermittent shortness of breath at rest, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite, ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, and decreased libido since starting a new, high-stress job.

History:
• Symptoms began after changing jobs (timeline not precisely stated; “since I changed my job”).  
• Headaches: intermittent, frontal, occur mainly at work while on laptop or in meetings; no aura; mild nausea; no radiation.  
• Palpitations: awareness of rapid heartbeat, especially in elevator and randomly ~once daily.  
• Shortness of breath: episodic, occurs while sitting at desk; not present during exercise.  
• Tingling: bilateral hands, described as “quick picking”; no lower-limb involvement.  
• Appetite decreased; ~5 lb unintended weight loss; clothes not noticeably looser; no external comments on weight change.  
• Loss of libido coincides with other symptoms.  
• Stress level rated 7–8/10 (baseline high due to law-firm environment).  
• Denies usual headaches prior to current episode.  
• No other associated neurological or systemic symptoms reported.

Past Medical History:
• “Hyperthyroidism” (patient report) – patient currently taking thyroxine. (Conflict noted: thyroxine typically used for hypothyroidism.)  
• No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
• Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• None reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer in London; mixed desk work and meetings.  
• Alcohol: ~2 glasses of wine once weekly.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (video consultation).

Investigations:
• Planned: Blood tests to check thyroid function (“thyroxine”) during upcoming in-person visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: New-onset intermittent headaches with mild nausea.
  – Plan: Schedule in-person visit for full neurologic and general exam; assess for tension vs migraine vs secondary causes.  

Issue 2: Palpitations and episodic shortness of breath.
  – Plan: In-person cardiovascular and respiratory examination; consider ECG and thyroid panel to rule out thyrotoxicosis or arrhythmia.  

Issue 3: Bilateral hand tingling.
  – Plan: Neurologic and musculoskeletal examination at visit; consider serum B12, glucose, thyroid tests if clinically indicated.  

Issue 4: Unintentional weight loss, reduced appetite, decreased libido.
  – Plan: Review thyroid status, screen for stress/anxiety/depression; consider basic metabolic panel and further endocrine tests based on initial findings.  

General Plan items:
• Patient to self-book face-to-face appointment via clinic app; clinician will document current history for hand-off.  
• No medications prescribed at this time pending physical evaluation and test results.  
• Provide reassurance; advise on stress-management techniques until review.  
• Follow-up: after examination and labs, or sooner if symptoms worsen (e.g., persistent palpitations, severe headache, visual changes, syncope).

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, objective physical findings, full medication list, formal allergy documentation.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient states “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine (used for hypothyroidism).  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional pauses/fillers; clinically relevant data obtainable.
